findings.title: Task 6 contradicts itself on informational events, and Task 8 covers only one of three `sdk_type` filters
findings.description:
Task 6 says an informational `RateLimitEvent` should be "continue[d] … without yielding it to the caller", and in the same sentence says to "let it flow to translation as normal". These are opposite behaviors. The slice design repeats the contradiction: D4 says informational events "must not reach translation", while the Data Flow section says the path "continues to translation".

The code makes the ambiguity matter. `agent.py:140` yields every parsed message, and `_handle_query_mode` and `_handle_client_mode` pass each one to `translate_sdk_message`. If informational events flow through, Task 4 turns them into `system` messages. Other consumers then see them:
- `src/squadron/review/review_client.py:263` and `src/squadron/pipeline/summary_oneshot.py:139` both use `(SDK_RESULT_TYPE, "tool_use", "tool_result")` as their skip list. Neither list contains `rate_limit_event`.
- Task 8 adds the type only to `sdk_session.dispatch`. Its grep step says to check for other lists, but gives no instruction to extend them.

Informational events could therefore leak into review prose, the same defect class as issue #23. Task 4 also doesn't say what the translated message's `content` should be, and review_client appends `response.content` to its output.

Fix: Task 6 should state one behavior. Either drop informational events in `_skip_unparseable` and don't yield them, or yield them and extend all three skip lists. Task 4 should specify the `content` value. Task 14's check that no rate-limit text appears in the artifact is a live check only, not a regression test.

findings.title: Commit markers are in the wrong format, appear after nearly every task, and several sit at red or regressed states
Test-with pattern is broken for the load-bearing tasks, and the task count is heavier than the slice needs
findings.description:
Tests for Tasks 6, 7 and 8 arrive in Tasks 10 and 11, with the shim deletion (Task 9) in between. Suggested restructure:
- Merge Task 8, a one-line change in `dispatch`, into Task 7. Both touch the same function in the same file.
- Move the `test_agent.py` rewrite and shim-test deletions (Task 10) to directly follow or merge with Tasks 6 and 9.
- Move the `test_sdk_session.py` rewrite (Task 11) to directly follow or merge with Task 7.
- Merge Task 12 into Task 13. Task 12 is verification-only and makes no changes. Its `pytest tests/providers/sdk/test_provider.py tests/metrology/test_audit_cli.py` run is a subset of Task 13's full-suite run.
- Consider merging Tasks 2+3 and 4+5. Each test task is small.

Together this takes the file from 16 tasks to about 9–10 for a slice rated 3/5 effort.

findings.title: Success Criterion 7 has no end-to-end test, and Task 3's substring test uses the fabricated form that criterion 9 forbids
findings.description:
Criterion 7 requires that a plain `ClaudeSDKError` containing `rate_limit` still triggers backoff. Task 10 rewrites every test that uses `ClaudeSDKError("rate_limit_event: ...")` onto a real `RateLimitEvent`. That removes the only integration tests of the retained substring path through the retry gate. Task 3 tests `_is_throttle` in isolation. It does not test that the gates in `agent.py` and `sdk_session.py` call it for this path.

Task 3 also uses the text `"rate_limit_event: slow down"` for that unit test. That is the fabricated `rate_limit_event` text criterion 9 is trying to eliminate. A genuine 429 would read differently.

Fix: Add at least one retained or new test where a plain `ClaudeSDKError` with 429-style text (containing `rate_limit` but not `rate_limit_event`) triggers backoff through the agent loop. Add the same for the `dispatch` loop if budget allows. Change Task 3's example text to match.

findings.title: `_is_throttle` is a private name imported across modules, which can fail pyright strict
findings.description:
Task 2 defines `_is_throttle` as a module-level private helper in `rate_limit.py`. Tasks 6 and 7 import it into `agent.py` and `sdk_session.py`. The Task 3 tests also import it from `rate_limit.py`. If the project runs pyright in strict mode, as the Python rules specify, `reportPrivateUsage` flags importing a name that starts with an underscore from another module. Task 13 requires zero pyright errors, so this would block the quality gate.

Fix: Name it `is_throttle` (public), or have Task 2 note the pyright constraint explicitly.

findings.title: Criterion 2 is only verified against `src`, and Task 12's rationale conflicts with the slice's affected-files list
findings.description:
Criterion 2 and walkthrough step 1 grep `src tests` for `install_rate_limit_parser_shim`. Task 9's success check greps only `src`. The grep for that symbol in tests is implicit in Task 10's deletion of the four shim tests, and it is never stated as a check.

The slice's affected-files list says `test_provider.py` and `test_audit_cli.py` are among the files requiring the criterion-9 rewrite, described as "shim install and rate-limit config plumbing". Task 12 concludes neither needs a rewrite. My grep of `tests/` supports Task 12: `test_audit_cli.py` has two hits, which are `detail="rate_limit_event: quota"` strings only, and `test_provider.py` has none. The task file is probably right and the slice text imprecise, but the task file never says it is deviating from the slice. Task 12 and Task 16 note it only as a DEVLOG item.

Fix: Add `grep -rn install_rate_limit_parser_shim src tests` to Task 9's success check. In Task 12, or the merged Task 13, state explicitly that this deviates from the slice's affected-files list.

findings.title: No load test or CI wiring task is required
findings.description: The slice restates no NFR and adds no new simulation, network or concurrency path. The retry loops and backoff schedule are unchanged. The absence of a `tests/load/` task and a CI gating task leaves no requirement unmet.
